function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below you’ll find two ways to spin‑up a **Google Compute Engine** VM that has:

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| OS   | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (`ubuntu-os-cloud/ubuntu-2004-focal-v20231102`) |
| GPU  | NVIDIA® RTX A6000 (24 GB) – one per instance |
| Machine type | Custom “n1” family (you can tweak CPU/RAM if you wish) |

> ⚠️  
> *GCP does **not** have “EC2”; that’s Amazon Web Services.*  
> In GCP we talk about **Compute Engine** VMs.  

---

### 1️⃣ Quick CLI way – `gcloud`

```bash
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# Create a custom n1 machine type with enough vCPU & RAM for your workload
MACHINE_TYPE="custom-8-32768"      # 8 vCPUs, 32 GiB memory

INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

GPU_COUNT=1          # One RTX A6000
GPU_TIER="standard"  # Standard tier supports RTX A6000

# Make sure the GPU quota exists first:
#   gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter='name~RTX-A6000'

gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
    --accelerator=count=$GPU_COUNT,type=nvidia-tesla-a100-$GPU_TIER \\
        # NOTE: Replace above with correct accelerator ID once available;
        #       currently GCP lists only Tesla series but RTX A6000 is under
        #       "nvidia-tesla-a100". Check via:
        #         gcloud compute accelerator-types describe nvidia-tesla-a100-standard-us-central1-a
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --boot-disk-size=50GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
    --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
    --tags=http-server,https-server
```

#### What each flag means

* `--machine-type`: Pick a custom size that fits your CPU/memory needs.  
* `--accelerator`: Attach the GPU(s); replace the accelerator type with the exact ID returned by `gcloud compute accelerator-types list`.  
* `--boot-disk-*`: Size/type of the boot volume.  
* `startup-script`: Optional shell script that runs at boot (e.g., install drivers).

> 👉 **Important:** Before running the command make sure you’ve enabled the **NVIDIA GPU Driver Installer** package in the Marketplace or plan to run `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y cuda-drivers`.

---

### 2️⃣ REST API approach

If you prefer programmatic creation (Python, curl, Terraform…), here’s the minimal JSON payload you’d POST to the Compute Engine endpoint:

```json
{
  "kind": "compute#instance",
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "description": "Ubuntu 20.04 + RTX A6000",
  "labels": {
    "env": "demo"
  },
  "disks": [
    {
      "deviceName": "bootdisk",
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage":
          "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "accessConfigs": [{ "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT"}],
      "subnetworks": ["global/networks/default"]
    }
  ],
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/custom-8-32768",
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType":
        "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100-standard"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    { "email":"default","scopes":["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"] }
  ]
}
```

Send it with OAuth 2.0 token:

```bash
curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<YOUR-PROJECT>/zones/us-central1-a/instances \
     -d @payload.json
```

Replace `<YOUR-PROJECT>` with your project id and adjust the `acceleratorType` field to match the actual resource ID shown by:

```bash
gcloud compute accelerator-types list --format=json
```

---

### 🚀 After Creation

Once the instance boots:

1. SSH into it:  
   ```bash
   gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-demo --zone us-central1-a
   ```
2. Install CUDA/NVIDIA driver (if not preinstalled):  
   ```bash
   sudo apt-get update
   sudo apt-get install -y linux-modules-extra-$(uname -r)
   sudo modprobe nvidia
   ```

Check GPU status:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

That should show the RTX A6000 ready for workloads! 🎉
